name: Pottery and ceramics classes
summary: How expats find pottery and ceramics studios in Singapore for hobby classes, kids’ workshops, and small-group wheel throwing — including condo mess limits and kiln-fired project timelines.
body:
Pottery is a popular humid-weather indoor hobby: wheel classes, hand-building, and glaze workshops. Studios provide kilns most home condos cannot. Expect multi-week project cycles — clay does not finish in one Grab-able evening.

## Formats
- Drop-in or term adult wheel classes
- Kids’ holiday hand-building camps
- Private groups and date-night sessions
- Membership studio access for experienced makers

Confirm whether fees include clay, firings, and glaze — surprise firing invoices are common.

## Practical constraints
Drying and firing queues stretch around festive peaks. Allergies to dust and glaze chemicals matter; ask about ventilation. Take-home unfired work may crack in air-con if rushed.

## How to choose
Visit the studio: wheel count, instructor attention, and safety briefings. Prefer clear make-up policies for travel weeks. For kids, check age minimums and whether parents stay. Instagram-perfect studios still need kiln reliability — ask about turnaround times before gifting deadlines.

## Practical tip
Wear clothes you can ruin and keep nails practical for wheel days. Book finishing firings early if you need mugs ready before home leave.
